findings.title: Timed shutdown can leave flusher worker processes running
findings.body: When `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the timeout, or when an earlier worker consumes the remaining deadline, this `break` exits the loop without terminating any remaining flusher processes. This is a regression from the single-process implementation, which always terminated its worker after waiting. During rebalances or shutdowns with a timeout, orphaned workers can continue polling and producing buffered segments while a replacement strategy is started, leading to duplicate producers and leaked Redis/Kafka connections. The timeout should stop waiting for each remaining worker but still terminate/clean up every worker.

findings.title: Negative --flusher-processes values crash strategy construction
findings.body: The new CLI option accepts any integer, but a negative `max_processes` is truthy and produces a negative `num_processes`. The process map is then empty, and assigning the first shard at line 66 raises a KeyError because `i % self.num_processes` has no corresponding map entry. An invalid deployment argument can therefore prevent the consumer from starting. Validate that the option is positive before constructing the map (and define or reject zero explicitly, rather than silently treating it as the default).

findings.title: The new process-limit test does not exercise multiprocessing
findings.body: Passing `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` makes `SpanFlusher` create `threading.Thread` workers instead of spawned processes. Consequently this test only checks the in-memory shard mapping and cannot detect failures in the new production path, including spawn-time serialization/initialization, per-process Redis access, worker shutdown, or producer behavior. Add a test that runs without `produce_to_pipe` and mocks the producer at a process-safe boundary, or otherwise explicitly tests the spawned-worker path.
